_readme: DATA FILE for tools/doc_stack_check.py. This is the ONE place a contributor adds a path.
Every entry carries a 'why' explaining what creates the path and who reads it.
Adding a legitimate new path: pick the block that says how the path comes into existence --
install_map     -> the installer copies it out of this bundle (evidence = the file exists here)
scaffold        -> the installer's scaffold step must mkdir/seed it in a fresh project
created_on_use  -> a skill writes it while it runs; absent until then, and that is correct
ignore          -> the project owns it (game code/assets); the doc stack never creates it
and add ONE entry with a one-line 'why'. Do not add matching logic to the .py file.
TWO RULES THAT LIVE IN THE .py, STATED HERE SO NOBODY IS SURPRISED BY THEM:
1. A reference containing a placeholder ({{X}}, <x>, [x]) or a literal '*' is a PATTERN,
not an addressable path. It is judged by its ROOT: 'docs/*.md' passes because docs/ is
real; 'agents/*.md' fails because in an installed project the agents live at
.claude/agents/. A pattern excuses only other patterns -- never a literal filename.
2. Never write a wildcard entry whose 'why' cannot name what creates THAT path. A
'docs/*.md -- top-level docs the skills produce' entry once sat in created_on_use and
silently absolved docs/director-gates.md and docs/agents-index.md, two real installed-
path drifts. Enumerate the genuine outputs instead; the list below is that enumeration.
THREE THINGS A 'why' MUST NOT DO:
a. Name a LINE NUMBER. Whys used to cite 'skills/day-one-patch/SKILL.md:92'; one round of
edits shifted the file by four lines and every citation pointed at blank space. Cite the
file and the section by name -- those survive an edit, line numbers do not.
b. Name a SKILL OR COMMAND THAT DOES NOT SHIP. A why saying '/ux-design writes this' is a
phantom laundered into the allow-list. Check skills/<name>/SKILL.md exists first; the
slash_commands block below is checked automatically, whys are checked by you.
c. Say 'the skills produce it' without naming which skill. See rule 2 above.

scan._why: The surfaces that COMMAND paths at a reader. If a doc here names a path, something must create it.

extraction._why: What counts as a path reference. Deliberately conservative: a candidate needs a directory component so prose words with dots are never mistaken for files.

root_files.CLAUDE.md: The one file a fresh session reads cold; the only doc-stack file addressed without a directory component.

engine_asset_suffixes._why: Engine/source/binary formats are always the USER's game content, never doc-stack files this bundle owes anyone.

reject_prefixes.res://: Godot resource URI -- addresses the user's game content, not the doc stack.
reject_prefixes.user://: Godot user-data URI -- runtime path, never a repo file.
reject_prefixes.uid://: Godot resource UID -- an identifier, not a path.
reject_prefixes.~/: User-level home path; the studio is project-local and never writes there.
reject_prefixes.@: Skill/plugin reference syntax (@skills/...), not a filesystem path.
reject_prefixes.$: Shell variable expansion, resolved at runtime.
reject_prefixes./: Leading slash is a slash-command (/help) or an absolute path outside the project.

install_map.why: install.sh: templates/ -> .claude/docs/templates/ -- document templates the authoring skills fill in.
install.sh: docs/ -> .claude/docs/ -- the reference library (skills-index, agents-index, workflow-catalog, gates).
install.sh: skills/ -> .claude/skills/ -- every workflow skill the user invokes.
install.sh: agents/*.md -> .claude/agents/, plus agents/engine-packs/<pack>/*.md when --engine is passed.
install.sh: hooks/ -> .claude/hooks/ -- session-start, skill-gate and validation hooks.
install.sh: rules/ -> .claude/rules/ -- per-domain coding rules loaded by the agents.
install.sh seeds the project CLAUDE.md from CLAUDE.md.template (never overwrites).
install.sh: tools/ -> <project>/tools/ -- runnable checkers the skills execute by path.

installer._why: Where the scaffold step must live, and how this check proves it exists rather than trusting it.

scaffold_region.why: The scaffold step must sit between these two markers in each installer script. Matching only inside the region stops an incidental mention in a copy comment from being read as coverage.

slash_commands._why: A '/command' in a doc is an instruction to RUN something, and is checked the same way a path is: skills/<name>/SKILL.md must exist or the instruction dead-ends. This list is the ONLY exemption, and every entry says why. It is deliberately short -- 'it is probably a built-in' is how five phantom gates (/story-done, /story-readiness, /smoke-check, /test-helpers, /test-evidence-review) survived a full phantom-path sweep invisible. The list is exactly as long as what is actually cited: an exemption with nothing to exempt reads as laundering, so entries are added when a citation needs one and removed when the citation goes.
